The Privacy Act of 1974 ( Pub. L. 93–579 , 88 Stat. 1896 , enacted December 31, 1974 , 5 U.S.C. § 552a ), a United States federal law , establishes a Code of Fair Information Practice that governs the collection, maintenance, use, and dissemination of personally identifiable information about individuals that is maintained in systems of records by federal agencies. [ 1 ] At its creation, it was meant to be an "American Bill of Rights on data." [ 2 ]
